newsitem.title: UK: Alliance posts solid first half results.
newsitem.headline: Alliance posts solid first half results.

text.p: Alliance & Leicester Plc, the British building society which converted to a bank in April, marked its first set of results as a publicly listed company with a three percent fall in pre-tax profits for the first half of 1997.
But the figure of 178 million pounds ($283 million) was after a 28 million pound charge for the costs of conversion and was ahead of analyst forecasts.

Underlying operating profits rose seven percent to 206 million pounds. The dividend was raised by 18 percent to 6.4 pence per share, representing around one third of the expected dividend for the year.
The company said the first-half performance provided a solid base for the the full year.
It expects the remainder of 1997 to see continued strong competition and higher interest rates than at the beginning of the year.
Alliance said it would compete strongly in its established markets, increase new activities in general insurance and leasing and use its financial strength to create value for shareholders.
The group's underlying cost:income ratio of the mortgage and investments sector, excluding conversion costs, fell to 45.3 percent from 48.2 percent in first half 1996.
The decline underlined the continuing commitment to improving the group's operating efficiency, it said.
Gross residential mortgage advances increased 53 percent to 1,422 million pounds, representing a four percent market share of total UK mortgage lending.

Competition in both the core mortgage and savings markets has continued to put pressure on the interest margins. Mortgages and investments contributed 128 million pounds to group operating profits up six million pounds on last year.
